_comment: Elbow-wrist tendinopathy corridor (tennis/golfer's elbow + wrist): stretch -> isometric -> loaded -> eccentric ladder; original instruction text authored in-house for Carryover.

exercises.name: Wrist Extensor Stretch
instructions: Stand tall and reach your affected arm straight out in front, palm facing down.
Keep the elbow fully straight, then use your other hand to gently bend the wrist so the fingers point toward the floor.
Angle the hand gently toward its little-finger side until you feel a comfortable pull along the top of the forearm — a stretch, never a sharp pain.
Hold steady without bouncing, then release slowly.

exercises.name: Wrist Flexor Stretch
instructions: Stand tall and reach your affected arm straight out in front, palm facing up, fingers pointing away from you.
Keep the elbow straight and use your other hand to draw the fingers back toward your body.
Feel the stretch along the inside of the forearm, from the wrist toward the elbow — ease off if anything pinches or tingles into the hand.
Hold the position quietly, then release with control.

exercises.name: Isometric Wrist Extension
instructions: Sit with your forearm resting along your thigh, palm down, hand and wrist just past the knee.
Place your other hand flat on top of the knuckles.
Try to lift the back of your hand toward the ceiling while the top hand blocks any movement — push at an effort that feels firm but stays comfortable at the elbow.
Keep breathing normally through the hold, then relax completely.

exercises.name: Towel Grip Squeeze
instructions: Sit tall and hold a small rolled towel in your affected hand, elbow bent and tucked at your side.
Squeeze the towel steadily, as if wringing water out with your fist alone.
Build to a firm effort that does not provoke sharp elbow pain, keeping the wrist in a straight, neutral line.
Hold the squeeze, then let the hand fully soften before the next one.

exercises.name: Towel Wring
instructions: Stand holding a rolled towel horizontally in front of you with both hands, elbows softly bent.
Twist the towel as if wringing out water — one hand turns forward while the other turns back.
Move slowly to the end of comfortable rotation, then reverse and twist the other way.
Keep the shoulders relaxed; the movement comes from the forearms, not from swinging the arms.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Forearm Rotation
instructions: Sit with your forearm supported along your thigh, wrist just past the knee, holding a light dumbbell by one end so it points up like a hammer.
Slowly rotate the forearm until the palm faces up.
Reverse and rotate until the palm faces down, keeping the elbow still against your side and letting the weight's leverage do the work.
Stay slow and controlled in both directions; if pain builds at the elbow, shorten the arc.

exercises.name: Band Wrist Extension
instructions: Sit with your forearm along your thigh, palm down, wrist just past the knee, and one end of a resistance band pinned under your foot.
Grip the other end of the band so it carries light tension in the start position.
Lift the back of your hand upward against the band as far as comfortable, keeping the forearm anchored on the thigh.
Lower back down slowly — the return should take longer than the lift.

exercises.name: Seated Hammer Curl
instructions: Sit tall holding a light dumbbell at your side, thumb pointing up so the weight stays vertical.
Keep the elbow tucked close to your ribs and curl the hand toward the shoulder.
Lower back down with control, finishing with the elbow fully straight each time.
Avoid swinging the trunk or shrugging the shoulder — the forearm does the work.

exercises.name: Eccentric Wrist Extension
instructions: Sit with your forearm along your thigh, palm down, holding a light dumbbell with the wrist just past the knee.
Use your free hand to help lift the back of the working hand up to the top position.
Take the helping hand away and lower the weight slowly on your own, letting the wrist bend down past neutral.
The slow lowering is the exercise — mild, familiar tendon soreness is acceptable, but sharp pain means lighten the load.

exercises.name: Eccentric Wrist Flexion
instructions: Sit with your forearm along your thigh, palm up, holding a light dumbbell with the wrist just past the knee.
Use your free hand to help curl the working wrist up to the top position.
Remove the helping hand and lower the weight slowly, letting the wrist open all the way down.

Keep the forearm resting on the thigh throughout — only the wrist moves, and the way down stays slow. Mild, familiar tendon soreness is acceptable, but stop and lighten the load if the pain turns sharp.

progressions.note: Add isometric loading once the stretch is held at end range with pain no higher than 2/10 on three consecutive days.
Move to band work when a 45-second firm press stays at or below 3/10 pain in three straight sessions.
Progress to eccentrics when a full band session produces no next-morning pain increase for a week.
Begin grip work once the stretch reaches a full comfortable range at 2/10 pain or less, with no tingling.
Start eccentric flexor loading when full-range wrings stay at or below 2/10 at the inner elbow during and the morning after for a full week.
Add wringing once a firm squeeze is held 30 seconds without symptoms rising above baseline afterward.
Load rotation with a dumbbell when full-range wrings in both directions stay under 3/10 during and after.
Add the curl when a full set of wrings causes no pain above 2/10 during or the morning after.
